title: text_ledger scan_c_like reports wrong line numbers for 1175 of 1899 JS comment units
claim: tools/audit/text_ledger.py:scan_c_like loses one line each time a non-template string literal stops at a newline (break before line += 1, i = j + 1 consumes it), so the `line` column of 1175 of the seat's 1899 JavaScript comment units does not hold the unit's text (tests/card.mjs 690, policy_lint.mjs 353); Python units, numbered by tokenize, are 0 of 1200.
mechanism: A quote inside a regex literal or a stray apostrophe opens a 'string' that ends at the newline; the newline is skipped without counting; the error accumulates down the file (card.mjs's DESIGN.md unit reports 10542, the text is at 10605). Ids are hashes, so `check` still passes and the defect is silent; a seat or fixer walking to a ledger row lands on the wrong code.

evidence.machine: box B12 (light seat), Linux x86_64, 4 vCPU, venv-ci python 3.14
evidence.contention_note: count; contention-immune (other seats on the box)

perturbation.change: --fixed: in scan_c_like, `line += 1` before the newline `break`, and on an escaped newline

null_control.note: the Python path (tokenize) carries no drift in either arm

metric_definition: JS/sh D5 comment units whose reported line does not contain the unit's first comment line, in the seat's cells.
phenomenon_property: Every unit text_ledger.py lists carries the line it starts on.
seam_rule: dev/audit/rounds/round11/D5/s8/ledger_lines.py (per-file RESULT lines; run over any cells list)
proposed_fix_scope: One-line instrument repair in scan_c_like (count the newline the string scan breaks on, and an escaped newline) plus a self-test arm with a quote in a regex literal; D6 string units share the scanner.
